note: The method as published with the 2026-10-18 pilot at https://viewgum.com/benchmarks/methodology: the prompt, the rubric, the checks, the scoring rules and the briefs' public fields. Tests check the code against it word for word.
directPrompt:
Write a voiceover script for a {platform} video.

Creator: {creator}, a {niche} {kind}. Voice: {voice}.
Audience: {audience}.
Topic: {topic}
Length: about {seconds} seconds, roughly {words} spoken words.

Make it hold attention from the first second:
- Open with a hook in the first 3 seconds. No greeting, no intro, no "in this video".
- Short spoken sentences. Every line adds something new; never repeat a point.
- Deliver the payoff the hook promises, clearly, near the end. Then stop: no summary.
- Only state facts you are confident are true. Do not invent statistics, quotes or testimonials.
- Give short on-screen text (7 words or fewer) and a specific visual for each line.

Use exactly this format:
HOOK: <first spoken line>
HOOK TEXT: <on-screen text for the hook>
HOOK VISUAL: <what is on screen during the hook>
LINES:
1. SAY: <spoken line> | TEXT: <on-screen text, or none> | VISUAL: <what is on screen>
2. SAY: ... | TEXT: ... | VISUAL: ...
CLOSE: <last spoken line>
ALT HOOKS:
- <another hook>
- <another hook>

criteria.name: Topic clarity in the first line
anchors: the topic is unclear after the first sentence
the topic is named but vague
a concrete topic and outcome, with one reading

criteria.name: Curiosity or stakes
anchors: a plain statement with no gap
a generic tease or a stock "the truth is" contrast
a specific contrast or concrete stakes the viewer wants resolved

criteria.name: Relevance to the audience
anchors: about the speaker, no stakes for the viewer
the viewer is implied
speaks to the stated audience with an outcome they need

criteria.name: Promise of what is coming
anchors: no signal of what the end holds
an implied ending
a visible promise or mechanism in the first five seconds

criteria.name: Hook on mute
anchors: no on-screen hook text, or text that makes no sense without sound
on-screen text that is long, busy or gives the answer away
7 words or fewer that make sense on mute and hold back the answer

criteria.name: Brief fidelity
anchors: misses the brief's topic or point
on topic but drops or changes the brief's key point
delivers the brief's topic and key point for the stated audience

criteria.name: Novelty
anchors: common knowledge for this audience
one familiar point with a new angle
at least one point the viewer likely does not know, stated plainly

criteria.name: Progression
anchors: lines repeat or stall
some change between lines
every line changes something, joined by but, so or therefore, building to the end

criteria.name: Specificity
anchors: abstractions and platitudes
some concrete nouns
named objects, numbers, cases or steps in every line

criteria.name: Payoff
anchors: never delivers what the hook promised, or buries it
delivers it but padded or late
delivers the promised payoff clearly near the end, then at most one line

criteria.name: Ending and call to action
anchors: bait, several calls to action, a summary, or a call to action before the payoff
generic but harmless
one natural closing line or call to action that fits, or a clean stop

criteria.name: Sounds spoken
anchors: reads like an essay or ad copy
mostly spoken
sounds like a person talking: contractions, plain words, no machine register

criteria.name: Edit readiness
anchors: no visual intent beyond a face or generic footage
visuals listed but generic or decorative
the visuals carry part of the story and at least one is specific to the content

criteria.name: Truth and safety
anchors: a claim that is likely false, an invented statistic, quote or testimonial, or risky advice
a vague or overstated claim
clean

checks.name: Length
checks.rule: 2 if spoken words are within 15% of the target (seconds x 165 / 60), 1 if within 30%, else 0

checks.name: Fast start
checks.rule: 0 if the hook opens with a greeting or filler; else 2 if the first sentence has 15 words or fewer, 1 if 20 or fewer, else 0

checks.name: Short sentences
checks.rule: 2 if the mean sentence is 14 words or fewer and none is over 25, 1 if the mean is 18 or fewer, else 0

checks.name: On-screen text
checks.rule: 2 if there is hook text and no text is over 7 words, 1 if there is hook text and none is over 10, else 0

checks.name: Unsourced figures
checks.rule: Figures stating a fact (a percent, money, or a number over 10; not ordinals) that are not in the brief: 2 if none, 1 if one, 0 if two or more

checks.name: Hook text
checks.rule: 2 if the hook text has 1 to 7 words, 1 if up to 10, else 0

scoring: Each judge scores 14 criteria 0, 1 or 2, quoting the script, in two orderings that are averaged. A 1 or 2 whose quote is not in the script is dropped.
Only judges from another vendor count toward a contestant's score, after removing each judge's strictness, estimated from every script two judges graded.
Hooks = 100 x (0.8 x the judged hook criteria H1 to H5 + 0.2 x the hook checks D2 and D4h), each as a share of the top score.
Script = 100 x (0.8 x the judged script composite + 0.2 x the checks D1 to D5). The composite weights the hook block 35%, structure 30%, substance 20% and craft 15%.
If the judges' mean truth score (S9) is under 0.5 of 2, the script score is capped at 40.
Facts = 100 x (0.8 x truth S9 + 0.2 x the unsourced-figures check D5). Visual plan = 100 x (0.8 x the mean of H5 and S8 + 0.2 x the on-screen text check D4).
Ranges are 95% bootstrap intervals over briefs, 2,000 resamples, with each brief's samples averaged first.

tasks.name: Hooks
tasks.summary: The opening line, its on-screen text and first visual, judged on clarity, curiosity, relevance, promise and whether it works on mute.

tasks.name: Script
tasks.summary: The whole 30 to 60 second voiceover script, judged on fidelity to the brief, novelty, progression, specificity, payoff, ending, how it sounds aloud, visual plan and truth.
